paragraphs: [Bava Metzia 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.93b.12) relates that Aivu deposited flax with Runya; Shevu (a thief’s name) came and snatched it from him. He came before Rav Nachman, who held him liable.

There, at [109a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.109a.17): Runya was Ravina’s tree-planter; Runya caused a loss, and Ravina dismissed him. Runya came before Rava and said to him, “Look, Master, at what he is doing to me.” He said to him, “He was right to do so.” In [Bava Batra 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.5a.1-3): Ravina surrounded Runya on his four sides — he came before Rava.[^1]

Hyman argues that we need not say that there were two Runyas or that he lived long, for the incident was at the end of Rav Nachman’s days, and Ravina was Rava’s student, and Rava was Rav Nachman’s distinguished student; or possibly it is Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.[^2]

notes.text: In the planter story, Runya caused a loss, Ravina dismissed him, and Runya appealed to Rava.

Hyman rests his argument for one Runya on the relative chronology of the teachers and suggests that the Rav Nachman in the flax case may have been Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak. The cases themselves give Rav Nachman, Ravina and Rava as named in the respective episodes.
